newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee seen heading for devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee seen heading for devaluation.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee is again under pressure and another devaluation is likely soon, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I see an 8.5 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar by December," Ashraf Rao, managing director of Dubai Exchange International, told Reuters.

Last week, Pakistan's central bank devalued the rupee by 7.86 percent against the dollar to 40.1200/40.3206, from 36.9700/37.1549 fixed on September 10. In the kerb market, the rupee fell to 42.70 from 40.55 on the eve of the devaluation.
On Tuesday, the rupee opened at 43.08 0.18 in the kerb market compared with 42.90 at its previous close.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan gave no reason for the devaluation but foreign exchange dealers attributed it to pressure by the International Monetary Fund aimed at restructuring the depressed economy and boosting exports.

Dealer Sikandar Glaxy said some banks were buying dollars encouraged by the central bank's offer of a 17 percent annual return and other concessions to banks bringing in foreign currency deposits until November 28.
Central bank governor Muhammad Yaqub has said banks placing foreign currency in a special deposit could withdraw an equivalent amount in rupees and earn a yield of 17 percent a year.
The central bank said the move was aimed at encouraging forex inflows to shore up depleting reserves. Forex reserves stood at $831 million, excluding gold, on October 3.
